title.en: The Quebec Act, the Loyalists and the first assemblies
title.fr: L'Acte de Québec, les loyalistes et les premières assemblées

text.en: The French-speaking Catholic people of the Province of Quebec were known as habitants or Canadiens.
text.fr: Les gens catholiques et francophones de la province de Québec étaient appelés habitants ou Canadiens.

source.quote: The French-speaking Catholic people, known as habitants or Canadiens

verification.evidence: Following the war, Great Britain renamed the colony the “Province of Quebec.” The French-speaking Catholic people, known as habitants or Canadiens

text.en: The Quebec Act gave Catholics freedom of religion, and it let them hold public office. At that time, Britain itself did not allow this.
text.fr: L'Acte de Québec a accordé la liberté de religion aux catholiques et leur a permis d'occuper des charges publiques. À l'époque, la Grande-Bretagne elle-même ne le permettait pas.

source.quote: It allowed religious freedom for Catholics and permitted them to hold public office, a practice not then allowed in Britain.

verification.evidence: the British Parliament passed the Quebec Act of 1774. … It allowed religious freedom for Catholics and permitted them to hold public office, a practice not then allowed in Britain.

text.en: The Quebec Act brought back French civil law, and it kept British criminal law in place.
text.fr: L'Acte de Québec a rétabli le droit civil français tout en conservant le droit criminel britannique.

source.quote: The Quebec Act restored French civil law while maintaining British criminal law.

verification.evidence: The Quebec Act restored French civil law while maintaining British criminal law.

text.en: Joseph Brant led thousands of Mohawk who were Loyalists into Canada.
text.fr: Joseph Brant a mené au Canada des milliers de Mohawks loyalistes.

source.quote: Joseph Brant led thousands of Loyalist Mohawk Indians into Canada.

verification.evidence: Joseph Brant led thousands of Loyalist Mohawk Indians into Canada.

text.en: About 3,000 black Loyalists, some free and some enslaved, came north hoping for a better life.
text.fr: Environ 3 000 loyalistes noirs, certains libres et d'autres esclaves, sont venus vers le nord dans l'espoir d'une vie meilleure.

source.quote: About 3,000 black Loyalists, freedmen and slaves, came north seeking a better life.

verification.evidence: About 3,000 black Loyalists, freedmen and slaves, came north seeking a better life.

text.en: The first assembly chosen by voters was elected in Halifax, Nova Scotia, in 1758.
text.fr: La première assemblée choisie par des électeurs a été élue à Halifax, en Nouvelle-Écosse, en 1758.

source.quote: The first representative assembly was elected in Halifax, Nova Scotia, in 1758.

verification.evidence: The first representative assembly was elected in Halifax, Nova Scotia, in 1758.

text.en: The Constitutional Act of 1791 split the Province of Quebec in two. One part was Upper Canada, which later became Ontario.
text.fr: L'Acte constitutionnel de 1791 a divisé la province de Québec en deux. L'une des parties était le Haut-Canada, qui est devenu plus tard l'Ontario.

source.quote: The Constitutional Act of 1791 divided the Province of Quebec into Upper Canada (later Ontario)

verification.evidence: The Constitutional Act of 1791 divided the Province of Quebec into Upper Canada (later Ontario), which was mainly Loyalist, Protestant and English-speaking, and Lower Canada (later Quebec), heavily Catholic and French-speaking.

text.en: The same Act gave the two Canadas their first legislative assemblies elected by the people.
text.fr: Le même Acte a donné aux deux Canadas leurs premières assemblées législatives élues par la population.

source.quote: The Act also granted to the Canadas, for the first time, legislative assemblies elected by the people.

verification.evidence: The Constitutional Act of 1791 divided the Province of Quebec into Upper Canada (later Ontario) … The Act also granted to the Canadas, for the first time, legislative assemblies elected by the people.
